gloss: volunteer work; community service; service activities

definitions.gloss: volunteer work; community service; service activities

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}に{参加|さんか}する。
{学校|がっこう}では{毎月|まいつき}{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}の{日|ひ}がある。
examples.english: At school, there is a community service day every month.

examples.japanese: {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}{後|ご}、{彼女|かのじょ}は{近所|きんじょ}の{清掃|せいそう}や{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}の{見守|みまも}りなど、さまざまな{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: After retirement, she has been engaged in various volunteer activities such as neighborhood cleaning and checking on the elderly.

notes:
A formal compound meaning volunteer or service activities performed for the benefit of the community without compensation. The word {奉仕|ほうし} (service, devotion) gives this term a slightly more formal and selfless nuance compared to the loanword ボランティア.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}に{参加|さんか}する: to participate in volunteer work
- {奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}に{取|と}り{組|く}む: to engage in service activities
- {地域|ちいき}{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}: community service
- {清掃|せいそう}{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}: cleanup volunteer work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ボランティア{活動|かつどう}: volunteer activities (more casual; the most common term in everyday speech)
- {社会貢献|しゃかいこうけん}: social contribution (broader; includes corporate philanthropy and paid work that benefits society)
- {慈善活動|じぜんかつどう}: charity work (focuses on helping the poor or disadvantaged)

USAGE:
{奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう} is preferred in formal writing, school contexts, and official announcements. ボランティア{活動|かつどう} is more natural in casual conversation. Schools in Japan often organize {奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう} as part of the curriculum.
